steps.title: Emit
steps.text: Ada emits a decision about decision:auth. It is checked, signed and appended: the store holds one record, and the thing has one head.

steps.title: Revise
steps.text: Ada revises it. B names A in prev, within the thing both are about. Nothing is edited: A is still there, superseded, and B is the head.

steps.title: Fork
steps.text: Bo, holding only A, revises it too. Two records name A, so the thing has two heads: a fork, shown as a conflict. C wins by content order, its later emitted, never by which arrived first; B is still shown.

steps.title: Merge
steps.text: Ada writes M naming both B and C. One head again. A merge is an emit whose prev holds two ids, not a verb of its own.

steps.title: Erase
steps.text: A had a secret pasted in. Ada's next revision, E, also erases A. A keeps its id, its signature and its place in the chain; only its opening goes, for every reader that holds E. decisions still counts five: count needs no payload.

steps.title: Any order
steps.text: Deliver the same five in any order, from any place, and every slot is the same. The set decides; that is what lets late arrivals, re-sent segments and two-way syncs agree.

steps.title: Less in view
steps.text: Cy's place holds E without its payload. Cy sees the same head, because prev is on the envelope and every reader holds envelopes. E's value is unread, and the result says so instead of guessing; the count, needing no payload, is still five.

steps.title: Tick
steps.text: At a boundary the vertex ticks: its result, covering exactly the five records it folded. Anyone holding them works out the same tick, so it can be cited. Ticks are settled, not built yet.

steps.title: Back to text
steps.text: A lens renders the head as a keyed section. Bo edits it; parsing finds one accepted edit, and applying it emits F, revising E. The edit is a record on the ground again: the loop closes. Applying edits as records is settled; the section round trip is proved.
